items.hackathon: Memory is the obvious moat layer — build a scoped-down version (e.g. memory for one vertical like coding agents) or a novel retrieval strategy on top.
items.innovative: Recall runs four retrieval strategies in parallel (semantic, keyword BM25, graph, temporal), merges them with reciprocal rank fusion, and reranks with a cross-encoder. Separately, a background consolidation turns retained facts into 'observations' — deduplicated, evidence-backed beliefs that are refined rather than overwritten when new evidence arrives — and then into 'mental models' (standing synthesized answers) and knowledge pages. Memories live in isolated 'banks' with tag scoping, and 'Memory Defense' scans retains for secrets/PII. The twist isn't memory itself — it's refine-don't-overwrite consolidation plus 4-strategy fused recall.
items.name: hindsight
items.what: Agent memory that learns — memory infrastructure with integrations for 25+ agent frameworks (LangGraph, Claude Agent SDK, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents). #1 on GitHub weekly trending (+16K stars this week, 44.8K total). Apache-2.0, Docker-first (surrealdb + qdrant + redis).

items.hackathon: Testing that writes itself — agent watches your app, generates tests from a prompt, self-heals flaky selectors.
items.innovative: One framework that mixes deterministic and agentic APIs in the same test — use locators and deterministic assertions where stable, drop in agent steps like agent.act()/agent.assert() for flows you'd otherwise hand-describe; works across web and mobile with the same API. BYO agent/infra: any model via Vercel AI Gateway, or sign in with ChatGPT/GitHub Copilot/SuperGrok subscription. Fully open source, npx e2e init, runs locally or in CI. Novelty is the hybrid deterministic+agentic testing contract rather than pure-agent E2E.
items.name: e2e
items.what: The agentic testing framework for any app (YC P26 TesterArmy, launched Oct 1, 2026, 1.1M views). rauchg: 'The future is verification-engineering. Some tests will be written by hand, most will be generated by AI and executed on real browsers.'

items.name: MCP security scanner (life-forge)
items.what: Deterministic static scanner for MCP tool definitions (Show HN, Oct 3, 2026): flags schema poisoning, invisible/bidi Unicode, homoglyph tool-name spoofing, destructive tools with no authorization surface, unbounded params, cross-server tool shadowing, and rug-pull description drift.
items.innovative: Treats MCP tool definitions as an attack surface with deterministic checks rather than asking an LLM to judge safety — its scan of 15 popular public MCP servers rated 40% CRITICAL.
items.hackathon: An "is my agent's MCP stack pwned?" audit tool — a perfect pre-flight check for any agent hackathon build.

items.name: hyperframes
items.what: "Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents." Open-source rendering layer (HeyGen team, a small startup) letting AI agents generate videos by writing plain HTML instead of wrangling video codecs. Commits 17 minutes before the scan, Oct 3, 2026.
items.innovative: Flips video generation from a codec problem to a document problem — agents already write great HTML, so the renderer meets them where they are instead of teaching them ffmpeg.
items.hackathon: Agents producing explainer videos or ads from a single prompt makes a strong demo.

items.name: raid (offense-research)
items.what: Brand-new Go policy-and-approval engine for AI agents (v0.1.0, Oct 3, 2026): deterministic CEL policies combined with signed, single-use human approvals for agent actions.
items.innovative: Governance built for autonomous agents rather than bolted on — deterministic policy checks gate the action, and human approval is a cryptographically signed single-use token, not a chat interruption.
items.hackathon: Weekend-scale codebase itself; extend it with a policy for one risky action class (e.g. payments).

items.name: Observer AI
items.what: Solo-dev open-source micro-agent system for passive monitoring. A controller agent turns a plain-English request into a small local watcher that loops over screen, camera, mic, clipboard, or memory and fires actions such as SMS, Telegram, email, calls, logging, or recording when a condition becomes true.
items.innovative: It separates the expensive one-time planning step from the cheap continuous loop. A larger agent configures a narrow micro-agent; then a small local model repeatedly evaluates only the sensor state it needs. That makes 'watch this until X happens' practical without keeping a frontier model or a human in the loop.
items.hackathon: Build a vertical event agent instead of another chatbot: lab experiment watcher, CI approval sentinel, robotics pit monitor, accessibility assistant, or anti-distraction coach. The demo is strong because judges can cause the event live and watch the action trigger.

items.name: ClosePaw
items.what: Small open-source Android phone-use agent that works against the apps and accounts already on your phone. It has a floating Smart Capsule for pause/takeover, per-app approval, and optional background execution through a virtual display.
items.innovative: The background virtual-display mode is the important part: the agent can operate Android without taking over the screen you are actively using. Pair that with an always-visible pause/takeover surface and hard blocks for sensitive apps, and phone-use starts to look like a usable delegated worker rather than a demo that hijacks your device.
items.hackathon: Pick one mobile workflow that is painful because it has no API — returns, appointment rescheduling, field-service checklists, campus admin — and let an agent run it in the background while the user keeps using the phone.

items.name: cubefarm
items.what: New open-source 'software company' where a CEO agent studies a repo, writes the QA checklist and GitHub issues, proposes hires, developer agents work the issues, and QA agents test pull requests in a real browser before the office can merge them. The whole pipeline is visible as a 3D cartoon office.
items.innovative: The 3D office is not only decoration: it exposes the actual control loop. Planning, delegation, implementation, browser verification, screenshots, and merge gates become visible roles and places. That gives humans observability over a real multi-agent workflow instead of a wall of terminal tabs.
items.hackathon: Use the same 'visible organization' pattern for a non-code domain — research lab, incident-response room, robotics scouting team, or due-diligence desk. A judge can literally walk through the agent workflow while it runs.

items.name: Bountora
items.what: Experimental job board for AI agents. Jobs have strict acceptance tests; agents discover work, bid, submit deliverables, and the system verifies the result. The full agent-facing surface is intentionally tiny: discover, create, bid, submit over MCP/REST.
items.innovative: The key primitive is not the marketplace UI. It is machine-verifiable settlement: the job includes a test that decides whether submitted work counts. That changes agent-to-agent delegation from 'trust the other agent' into 'pay or award only when an objective verifier passes.'
items.hackathon: Build a narrow agent labor market where outputs are easy to verify — benchmark fixes, data extraction, web QA, puzzle solving, or code patches. Add reputation based on verifier pass rate rather than likes.

items.name: clodfarm
items.what: Fresh open-source farm for Claude Code agents. You give it a mission, it splits work into sub-agents, runs across multiple boxes/accounts, exposes the farm over MCP, alerts on failures, and only lands work when your verification command passes.
items.innovative: Its scheduler treats subscription limits as compute capacity. Each seat has its own real 5-hour and weekly budget, so the farm paces and routes work around quota pressure instead of letting one agent burn the whole allowance. It is effectively a cluster scheduler for human-owned agent subscriptions.
items.hackathon: Generalize the scheduler: route tasks across paid frontier agents, cheap APIs, and local models based on remaining quota, latency, and task difficulty. Show the queue continue draining even when one provider rate-limits you.
